status: design only; wait for iteration017 completion
hypothesis: Expose a separate opt-in digit_implicit_gemm algorithm using four fused K6 gather/matmul calls, static digit weights/topology and the incumbent epilogue. Default remains unchanged until application validation.
implementation: Vendor only the required Apache-2.0 K6 layer and four kernels with notices and explicit pinned provenance; no full encoder dependency.

Prepare BF16 digit weights using existing public preparation, then cache two FP32 weight views and zero bias for prototype-equivalent arithmetic. Explicit static preparation API builds plans and index pages before timing.
Cache static topology plans by actual topology object plus row chunk and grid, never by shape alone; no feature-value caches.
Use bounded tile-aligned row chunks, physical multicast guard, fixed HiFi3, dead_skip=False and FP32 outputs. Support requested FP32 final output too.

All-channel wide/infeasible cases and unaligned interior chunks explicitly fall back to digit_explicit_gemm; report selected path and reason. Initial shape-only speed dispatch can be restricted to independently confirmed shapes.
Add independent work model for four fused products with active tap skips, no DRAM im2col, FP32 weight multicast and redundant output tables; requested bytes are not physical traffic.
Extend candidate source integrity hash to .hpp/.h so included gather helper is protected. Include vendors in installed package data.
Check all36 including fallback, BF16/FP32 output/cancellation, topology reuse, missing/repeated neighbors, changed features, ragged channels and many row chunks; replay workspace.
Three paired rounds on narrow and largest, plus a fallback control. Small shapes and 128→512 currently screen slower; retain records.
Integrate shape/texture decoders through prepared scratch adapter, preserve strict saved CPU quality gates and report any application failures.
later_fusion: One four-product kernel can share both gathered digit tables, weight loads and output assembly; remove four redundant BF16 table outputs.
Channel partitioning needed before claiming wide-layer support.
limits: Iteration017 is still running; no integration or promotion yet

The 48 integer-product checks match incumbent bitwise; exact CPU integer-dot equality was an overstrong assumption and failed for both incumbent and prototype. Never silently relabel those failed checks.
